Let \(q=3^r\). The answer is

\[
\boxed{
M_r=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{5q^3-q^2-3q+3}{8},& r\ \text{odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{7q^3+5q^2-7q+3}{12},& r\ \text{even}.
\end{cases}}
\]

**Solution.**

A Lagrangian graph \(L=\{x+Sx:x\in E\}\) is Lagrangian exactly when \(S=S^T\). The condition \(\jmath(L)=L\) forces \(S\) to commute with \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)\), hence

\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}
1&0&a&0\\
0&c&0&d\\
a&0&b&0\\
0&d&0&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The determinant condition becomes

\[
b-a^2+c-d^2=-1. \tag{1}
\]

For \(u_t=(1,t,t^2,t^3)^T\), the condition \(\rho_t(L)\cap F=0\) is equivalent to

\[
u_t^T S u_t\ne 0
\]

for all \(t\in\mathbb F_q\). Indeed, if \(z=x+Sx\in L\), then the \(E\)-part of \(\rho_t(z)\) is zero precisely when \(x\) is a scalar multiple of \(u_t\), and then the remaining obstruction is exactly \(u_t^T S u_t=0\).

Now

\[
u_t^T S u_t=t^6+(b+2d)t^4+(2a+c)t^2+1.
\]

Put

\[
A=b+2d,\qquad B=2a+c,\qquad C=A+B+1.
\]

Since \(2=-1\) in characteristic \(3\), equation (1) becomes

\[
a^2-a+d^2-d=C. \tag{2}
\]

For fixed \(C\), the number of pairs \((a,d)\) satisfying (2) is the representation number of

\[
X^2+Y^2=C-1,
\]

after completing squares. Hence

\[
N(C)=
\begin{cases}
1,&r\text{ odd and }C=1,\\
q+1,&r\text{ odd and }C\ne1,\\
2q-1,&r\text{ even and }C=1,\\
q-1,&r\text{ even and }C\ne1.
\end{cases}
\]

It remains to count, for fixed \(C\), the number \(K(C)\) of \(A\in\mathbb F_q\) such that

\[
g_{A,C}(y)=y^3+Ay^2+(C-1-A)y+1
\]

has no root among the squares \(y=t^2\). Note \(y=0\) is never a root.

For fixed \(C\), a square root \(y\ne0,1\) determines a unique bad value of \(A\), while \(y=1\) is a root exactly when \(C=-1\). Thus \(K(-1)=0\). Inclusion-exclusion over the nonzero square set \(Q\), \(|Q|=(q-1)/2\), gives

\[
\sum_C K(C)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{5q^2+3}{8},&r\text{ odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{7q^2+4q-3}{12},&r\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]

Also, for \(C=1\),

\[
K(1)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{3(q+1)}4,&r\text{ odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{2q}{3},&r\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]

These follow from the explicit bad-value map

\[
A=-\frac{(y+1)^3}{y(y-1)},\qquad y\in Q,\ y\ne1,
\]

whose image size is \((q-3)/4\) when \(-1\) is nonsquare and \(q/3\) when \(-1\) is square.

Therefore

\[
M_r=\sum_C N(C)K(C).
\]

If \(r\) is odd,

\[
M_r=(q+1)\sum_CK(C)-qK(1)
=(q+1)\frac{5q^2+3}{8}-q\frac{3(q+1)}4
=\frac{5q^3-q^2-3q+3}{8}.
\]

If \(r\) is even,

\[
M_r=(q-1)\sum_CK(C)+qK(1)
=(q-1)\frac{7q^2+4q-3}{12}+q\frac{2q}{3}
=\frac{7q^3+5q^2-7q+3}{12}.
\]

Thus, with \(q=3^r\),

\[
\boxed{
M_r=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{5\cdot 3^{3r}-3^{2r}-3\cdot 3^r+3}{8},& r\ \mathrm{odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{7\cdot 3^{3r}+5\cdot 3^{2r}-7\cdot 3^r+3}{12},& r\ \mathrm{even}.
\end{cases}}
\]
